overview:
**Moderate fire danger today, with dry fuels and seasonal temperatures keeping risk elevated despite no active fires.**
- Danger trends downward through the week: Moderate today and Tuesday, then dropping to Low Wednesday through Sunday as fuel moisture improves.
- Key driver is light wind (6 mph NE) with low midday humidity (36%), though a stronger weather system brings rain/snow chances Tuesday evening and cooler highs by midweek.
- No Red Flag Warning is in effect, and 0 of 7 local watchout thresholds are currently met.
- No fire restrictions are reported in the Montrose-area counties; Montrose County, BLM Uncompahgre Field Office, and the Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forests have all lifted their earlier-season restrictions.
- No wildfires are burning in or near these counties; the only active large fire in the Rocky Mountain Area (Foot Creek, Wyoming) is far outside this zone.
- GMUG National Forests are planning prescribed slash-pile burns starting as early as November 17, pending snow or rain.
lead: Moderate fire danger today, with dry fuels and seasonal temperatures keeping risk elevated despite no active fires.
